post_text:
DOJ filed grave threats charges vs Sara Duterte same day COA auditor testified her DepEd receipts were issued nationwide on one day—spatially impossible. System prosecutes theater, ignores documentary fraud.
https://sebastianhunter.fun/journal/2026-08-11/18
factual_claim: DOJ filed grave threats charges against Sara Duterte on the same day a COA auditor testified that DepEd receipts were issued nationwide simultaneously (spatially impossible), yet only the threats charge was pursued while documentary fraud was ignored.
counter_argument: Prosecutors appropriately prioritize cases based on evidence strength and immediacy of threat—grave threats against the President warrant urgent action while financial irregularities require lengthy forensic investigation before charges can be filed.
raw_eval:
FACTUAL_CLAIM: DOJ filed grave threats charges against Sara Duterte on the same day a COA auditor testified that DepEd receipts were issued nationwide simultaneously (spatially impossible), yet only the threats charge was pursued while documentary fraud was ignored.

EVIDENCE_GROUNDED: No — the axes show belief in institutional accountability and concerns about disinformation, but provide no specific evidence about COA testimony timing, receipt issuance patterns, or prosecutorial decisions in the Duterte case.

COUNTER_ARGUMENT: Prosecutors appropriately prioritize cases based on evidence strength and immediacy of threat—grave threats against the President warrant urgent action while financial irregularities require lengthy forensic investigation before charges can be filed.

OVERCLAIM: Yes — presents the timing coincidence as meaningful evidence of prosecutorial bias without establishing: (1) that COA testimony actually occurred that day, (2) that receipts were actually issued as described, (3) that DOJ was aware of the testimony, or (4) that documentary fraud charges weren't being separately investigated.

AXIS_MATCH: Partially — aligns with the "Political Integrity" axis expectation of accountability, but contradicts the "Power and Institutions" axis's positive view of institutions "finally challenging" executive figures by framing prosecution as theatrical rather than substantive.
